items.text: Lifetime, ownership, RAII, debugging. Diagnose dangling references, double deletion and use-after-free in small examples. RAII: file-handle owner that releases on normal return and exceptions.
Time/space complexity: explain linear, nested, logarithmic, and extra-storage costs.
Arrays/vectors/strings: second-largest distinct element, move zeros, string counts.
Requirements and constraints: inputs, outputs, rates, latency, memory, expected failures.

Robot architecture: sensing, estimation, planning, control, actuation and feedback.
ROS 2 packages: workspaces, ament_cmake, colcon, dependencies, interfaces, launch, parameters.

skills.plain: Stack/heap/storage duration; pointers/references; const; object lifetime; ownership versus borrowing; undefined behavior. Checkpoint: diagnose dangling references, double deletion, and use-after-free in small examples.

skills.skill: Copy/move, RAII, smart pointers, Rule of Zero/Three/Five
skills.plain: Value categories; copy/move constructors and assignment; moved-from states; std::move; RAII; unique_ptr/shared_ptr/weak_ptr; Rule of Zero/Three/Five. Checkpoint: write a buffer with deep copy and move, then replace manual ownership with a standard container. Explain when shared ownership is justified.

std::forward and forwarding references; overload resolution basics; noexcept; exception guarantees; destructor behavior. Checkpoint: write a forwarding wrapper and explain which constructor is called in test cases. Demonstrate cleanup on failure.

vector, array, string, string_view, span where supported, map/unordered_map, set/unordered_set, deque; iterators and invalidation; algorithms; comparators. Checkpoint: choose containers for small tasks and explain complexity, invalidation, and borrowed-view lifetimes.

Functions/lambdas/captures; templates; optional/variant; virtual functions/destructors; slicing; composition versus inheritance. Checkpoint: implement a small polymorphic interface and compare a callable-based alternative.

skills.skill: Threads, locks, condition variables, bounded queues
skills.plain: Threads; mutexes; scoped locking; condition variables; predicates; bounded queues; clean shutdown; races/deadlocks. Checkpoint: implement and test a bounded producer-consumer queue with cancellation.

skills.skill: Linux, Git, CMake, colcon, tests, GDB, sanitizers, CI
skills.plain: Linux shell; processes/signals; exit status; Git; CMake targets/linking; colcon; unit/integration tests; GDB; ASan/UBSan; basic CI. Checkpoint: build from a clean checkout, debug a crash, and reproduce a failed test.

skills.skill: Atomics, futures, jthread, profiling, linking and ABI
skills.window: P0 awareness, P1 depth · W6–12, M4–6
skills.plain: Atomics versus locks; futures/promises; jthread/stop tokens where supported; CPU/cache/allocations; profiling; compilation/linking/ODR/ABI. Checkpoint: explain basic atomic-counter use and use a profiler before proposing an optimization.

skills.skill: Concepts, type erasure, CRTP, CMake packaging
skills.plain: Concepts; template constraints; type erasure; CRTP; object layout; advanced exception safety; CMake packaging; cross-compilation basics. Checkpoint: build a small reusable library with a documented interface and tests.
Memory ordering depth; advanced concurrency; allocators; real-time allocation strategies; deeper ABI/plugin compatibility. Learn in response to measured problems or target-role requirements.

Checkpoint: tf2, map/odom/base_link, URDF/Xacro, SDF awareness, timestamps, simulation clocks, stale transforms.
Checkpoint: ROS CLI, RViz, rosbag2, recording metadata, replaying monitor inputs.
Checkpoint: Differential drive, odometry, feedback, saturation, PID, control-loop timing.
Checkpoint: Localization vs SLAM, maps/costmaps, global planner/local controller, recovery behavior; integrate Nav2.
Checkpoint: Stale data, cancellation, lost processes, request-to-stop vs actual stop verification.
Checkpoint: Registration, robot status, assignment, battery/charging, shared resources, disconnection, duplicate tasks.
Checkpoint: Fleet adapters, task integration, scheduling/traffic, state reporting, recovery.
Checkpoint: Versions/configuration, telemetry, offline operation, access control, staged updates, rollback.
Demonstration: Fixed/variable steps, wall/simulation/steady clocks, pause/step/reset, real-time factor.
Demonstration: Pin versions/configuration, record seeds and inputs, repeat runs; describe remaining nondeterminism.
Demonstration: Geometry, frames, collision, joints, mass, inertia, units.

skills.plain: Demonstration: Rate, timestamps, latency, noise, dropouts, calibration, ground truth.

skills.plain: Demonstration: Connect sensors and commands; study plugin interfaces and lifecycle.
Demonstration: Requirements, pass/fail thresholds, tolerances, failures, regression tests.

skills.window: P0 measurement W10–12; P1 tuning M4–6
skills.plain: Demonstration: CPU/GPU, memory, rendering cost, headless throughput, bottlenecks.

skills.window: P0 awareness W10–12; P1 depth M4–6
skills.plain: Demonstration: Define intended use, model limits, sensitivity, and comparison with measurements.

skills.window: P0 basic W4–12; P1 depth M4–6
skills.plain: Demonstration: One existing robot/world, ROS bridge, sensors, resets, headless runs, automated checks.
Demonstration: Hardware compatibility first; robot import, USD scene basics, ROS bridge, sensors, automated experiment.

skills.window: P2, M9–12 or earlier for a specific role
skills.plain: Demonstration: Actors/components, transforms, C++ modules, ticking, collision/physics, external communication, build/package workflow.
Demonstration: Robot learning and reinforcement learning foundations; only after a relevant role/project is selected.
Demonstration: DIS/HLA concepts, distributed entity state, time synchronization, coordinate systems; small unclassified interoperability demo.
The robot performs the simple motion task within specified position/time tolerances.
The relay drops supervisor input; the supervisor reacts; independent simulator state verifies the expected stopping behavior.
Cancellation interrupts an active task, the robot reaches the expected stopped condition, and resources/processes are cleaned up.

skills.skill: Release demo: bug, failing test, fix
skills.plain: At the first release, demonstrate a deliberately introduced bug, a failing test, your fix, and the test passing again.
Keep a short record of three real debugging investigations.

skills.window: Build/use W3–6; first focused contribution W7–12; continue through the year
skills.plain: Primary first target. Investigate: reproducible recorder/player defects, regression tests, lifecycle/error handling, timestamp/storage behavior.

skills.window: Use in Q1; targeted contribution M4–6
skills.plain: Investigate: narrow integration/system issues, reset/pause cases, sensor/configuration tests, later plugin fixes.
Investigate: adapter tests, state handling, configuration validation, reproducible integration failures.
Investigate: public extension examples/tests, ROS integration, imports, reproducibility improvements.
